subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should #38730 remain the umbrella until both high-frequency warning and cron-session retention work are resolved, or should maintainers split the remaining guardrails into narrower canonical issues now?
rationale: The gaps are source-backed, but warning thresholds, context-warning policy, and base-session cleanup semantics require maintainer product and compatibility intent before automation should create another fix lane.

options.title: Keep umbrella open
options.body: Use #38730 to coordinate the warning and retention slices, then split only leftover context-threshold or sessions-cleanup work after current related PRs are resolved.

options.title: Split remaining guardrails
options.body: Create or confirm narrower canonical issues for context warnings and sessions cleanup, and let each PR close only its own scoped slice.

options.title: Reject fixed warning threshold
options.body: If a sub-30-minute advisory is not desired, close or narrow the warning path while keeping retention cleanup as the primary bug track.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella open
recommendation.body: Use #38730 to coordinate the warning and retention slices, then split only leftover context-threshold or sessions-cleanup work after current related PRs are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: gumadeiras is the clearest owner signal for the cron/session pruning contract that drives the most compatibility-sensitive unresolved decision.
